What pulls the casing of a Franki pile down into the ground?
The concrete plug rammed inside the tube, through friction
Hammer blows on the top of the tube
The soil pumped out of the inside of the tube
The dry concrete placed in the bottom of the tube is rammed inside the tube by the 3 t drop hammer; through friction the plug drags the tube down with it – so neither soil nor water gets into it.
What is the “bulb” of a Franki pile?
The widened concrete body rammed out at the base
The cap above the pile head
The lower, conical end of the casing
A cracked zone forming along the shaft
When only 30–40 cm of concrete is left in the tube, further batches are rammed out: the compacted concrete base greatly increases the bearing capacity.
What resistance can be achieved with a Franki pile?
A Franki pile is at most 16–18 m long, approx. 60 cm in diameter because of the displacement, and a resistance of 2000–3000 kN can be achieved with it.
What happens to the soil when a (displacement) screw pile is drilled?
The drilling head pushes it aside and compacts it; hardly any spoil comes up
The auger brings the whole soil volume to the surface
The soil is removed by underwater dredging
The special head pushes aside and compacts the soil around itself while drilling. Only a little spoil comes to the surface – it does not need to be removed.
Which resistance increases primarily for a cast-in-place screw pile because of the compaction?
The tensile strength of the pile
Neither – only the strength of the concrete increases
For a precast (driven) pile both the base and the shaft resistance increase, for a cast-in-place screw pile primarily the shaft resistance.
How does the reinforcement get into a screw pile?
It is vibrated down into the fresh concrete
It is driven into the ground before drilling
It goes down inside the drill stem together with the drilling head
It is drilled in after the concrete has hardened
Concreting takes place through the drill stem while the stem is rotated and withdrawn; the prefabricated reinforcement cage is then vibrated down into the fresh concrete.
What are the usual diameter and the maximum length of screw piles?
The usual diameter is 300–600 mm, and the maximum length approx. 20 m. The lower structural capacity due to the smaller diameter may limit its spread.
Which screw pile system leaves a threaded shaft?
Smooth-shaft systems are e.g. Omega, Fundex, De Waal and CHD; Screwsol has a threaded shaft. CFA is not a displacement pile but a replacement (at most partial displacement) bored pile.
In which soil is the displacement screw pile least suitable?
In very dense gravel, hard clay
The technology is popular in loose to medium-dense granular, intermediate and soft–firm cohesive soil. In very dense, hard soil the head cannot push the soil aside.
